backend.image_note: purpose-built court image: the Debian bookworm glusterfs-server/glusterfs-client packages are baked in at build time because apt-get cannot run inside the court's cap-drop=ALL containers
backend.topology: one glusterd + one brick (single-brick distributed volume) in one server container; two independent FUSE client processes in two containers
backend.brick: /data/brick1 on a host bind mount, mode 0777

volume_options_changed.nfs.disable: on (Debian does not ship the NFS xlator; without it glusterd fails the start commit with 'DL open failed ... nfs/server.so')

backend.label: SINGLE HOST, one brick, one volume, TWO client processes, one writer at a time. Not a fleet, not multi-node, not replicated, not a cloud result. The brick is a host directory, so no media or power-loss claim is made.

why_capabilities: SYS_ADMIN: the brick stores metadata in trusted.glusterfs.* xattrs, which require it; without it `gluster volume create` fails with 'Setting extended attributes failed, reason: Operation not permitted'

DAC_OVERRIDE: the posix translator creates the `.glusterfs` handle directory with mode 0600 and descends into it as root; without the capability the brick aborts on '/data/brick1/.glusterfs/indices/xattrop: Failed to create [Permission denied]'

clients.why_capabilities: the Gluster FUSE client mounts through /dev/fuse; SYS_ADMIN is the minimum mount capability

arms.label: reduced
arms.durability: a completed write has fsynced the file (A-E) or atomically replaced the manifest (N); GlusterFS forwards fsync to the brick, which fsyncs the backing host file

close_to_open.method: writer does dd conv=fsync, the peer polls a fresh open+read for a matching SHA-256 at 10 ms resolution; the value is a ceiling on visibility latency

in_place_rewrite.method: A replaces the file atomically; B polls head -c 17 until it sees the new prefix
in_place_rewrite.why: GlusterFS guarantees close-to-open consistency; attribute caching is bounded by the client's md-cache/stat-prefetch timeouts

n_client_failure.method: client A writes 1 MiB chunks, each fsynced and its SHA-256 acknowledged to a container-local log, until the write fails; client A's GlusterFS FUSE process is SIGKILLed mid-write; client B reads every acknowledged chunk; a fresh client A mounts the volume again and reads them too
n_client_failure.kill: SIGKILL of the GlusterFS FUSE client process in client A while the writer was still running; acknowledged-before-kill=8 acknowledged-final=9 write-failed-at-chunk=10
n_client_failure.rule: every acknowledged (fsynced) chunk must read back intact on the peer; bytes beyond the last acknowledgement are unacknowledged and are reported, not counted as a loss

non_claims: one host, one brick, one volume, two client processes, one writer at a time; not a fleet, cluster, replicated or multi-node result
single-brick distributed volume only; no replica, disperse, distributed-replicate or geo-replication volume was measured
no NFS or SMB access; no Gluster NFS (the xlator is absent from the Debian packages and is disabled)
no media, power-loss or host-cache-loss claim; the failure test kills a client process, not a machine or a disk
no claim about GlusterFS versions other than the packaged 10.3 recorded here
